end.summary:
Aditya practised naming cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere in toys and objects.
They identified a ball as a sphere and a cube as having flat faces.
They corrected the idea that every box is a cube, noting that a matchbox has shorter sides.
They identified a glue stick as a cylinder with two flat faces.
They still mixed up whether a solid’s name changes when it is turned or placed differently.
end.parentNote: Asha practised matching everyday objects with solid shapes and sorting flat and curved faces. Aditya used visible features such as a ball’s round surface and a cylinder’s circular ends; they also corrected the matchbox example by checking side lengths. The idea that turning a shape changes its name was not corrected by the end, so at home you can turn a toy or object and ask, “Did its shape change, or only its position?”
